overall.pooledNote: Pooled over five different starting conditions: a mixture, not an estimate for any single rule set.

heterogeneity.note: Seeded permutation test (chi-square statistic) of first-mover wins across the five conditions, decisive games only. Exploratory: five conditions screened at once, no correction for multiple looks.

C1.note: plus = games where the first mover won in C1 but not in C0 (same seed and first mover); minus = the reverse

C2.note: plus = games where the first mover won in C2 but not in C0 (same seed and first mover); minus = the reverse

C3.note: plus = games where the first mover won in C3 but not in C0 (same seed and first mover); minus = the reverse

C4.note: plus = games where the first mover won in C4 but not in C0 (same seed and first mover); minus = the reverse

perCondition.note: With 20 decisive games a first-mover share must reach at least this many wins (75%) before an exact test rejects a 50/50 split at 5%, and a 95% interval is roughly +/- 20 points wide. Smaller real advantages are invisible at this sample size.

findings.text: C0 (3/3): first mover won 12/20 (60%, 95% CI 39%–78%, exact p vs 50% = 0.503). The interval includes 50%: no reliable first-mover effect at n = 20. Mean length 16.8 turns (95% CI 7.998–25.602), turn-limit rate 15%.

C1 (2/2): first mover won 13/20 (65%, 95% CI 43%–82%, exact p vs 50% = 0.263). The interval includes 50%: no reliable first-mover effect at n = 20. Mean length 9.45 turns (95% CI 7.619–11.281), turn-limit rate 0%.

C2 (4/4): first mover won 12/20 (60%, 95% CI 39%–78%, exact p vs 50% = 0.503). The interval includes 50%: no reliable first-mover effect at n = 20. Mean length 18.9 turns (95% CI 11.99–25.81), turn-limit rate 10%.

C3 (3/2): first mover won 10/20 (50%, 95% CI 30%–70%, exact p vs 50% = 1). The interval includes 50%: no reliable first-mover effect at n = 20. Mean length 15.7 turns (95% CI 8.419–22.981), turn-limit rate 10%.

C3: the side that started with more pieces won 10/20 (50%, 95% CI 30%–70%, exact p vs 50% = 1). More pieces also means more actions per turn and a larger victory requirement, so this is the effect of the whole package, not of piece count alone.

C4 (2/3): first mover won 17/20 (85%, 95% CI 64%–95%, exact p vs 50% = 0.003). The interval excludes 50%: an exploratory first-mover signal, to be re-tested on fresh seeds. Mean length 15.85 turns (95% CI 8.498–23.202), turn-limit rate 10%.

C4: the side that started with more pieces won 3/20 (15%, 95% CI 5%–36%, exact p vs 50% = 0.003). More pieces also means more actions per turn and a larger victory requirement, so this is the effect of the whole package, not of piece count alone.
All 100 games pooled: first mover won 64/100 (64%, 95% CI 54%–73%, exact p vs 50% = 0.007). Pooled across different rules, so it only says whether a first-mover tendency shows up broadly.

Do the five conditions differ in first-mover win rate? Permutation test p = 0.243. No evidence that starting piece count changes first-mover advantage at this sample size. This is absence of evidence, not evidence of no effect.

C1 vs C0 on the same seed and first mover: first-mover outcome flipped toward the first mover in 5 pairs and away in 4 (exact sign test p = 1). RNG trajectories: 1/20 games never diverged from the reference RNG sequence, so pairs share a seed but not a game.

C2 vs C0 on the same seed and first mover: first-mover outcome flipped toward the first mover in 4 pairs and away in 4 (exact sign test p = 1). RNG trajectories: 1/20 games never diverged from the reference RNG sequence, so pairs share a seed but not a game.

C3 vs C0 on the same seed and first mover: first-mover outcome flipped toward the first mover in 3 pairs and away in 5 (exact sign test p = 0.727). RNG trajectories: 0/20 games never diverged from the reference RNG sequence, so pairs share a seed but not a game.

C4 vs C0 on the same seed and first mover: first-mover outcome flipped toward the first mover in 8 pairs and away in 3 (exact sign test p = 0.227). RNG trajectories: 0/20 games never diverged from the reference RNG sequence, so pairs share a seed but not a game.
Game length (mean turns): C0 16.8, C1 9.45, C2 18.9, C3 15.7, C4 15.85. Fewer pieces means fewer actions per turn but also fewer pieces to bring across.

Conveyor-belt moves (a piece stepping on its own side's trap and being carried forward): C0 14.65/game (more-conveyor side won 10/18); C1 11.3/game (more-conveyor side won 11/20); C2 17.45/game (more-conveyor side won 8/19); C3 12.65/game (more-conveyor side won 11/18); C4 13.35/game (more-conveyor side won 11/18). An association with winning is not proof that conveyors cause wins: stronger positions also create more chances to use them.
Both sides use the same deterministic planner and weights, so "Human side" and "AI side" are board directions, not different players. Results describe this planner playing itself, not human play.
These 100 games are exploratory. They were looked at to form hypotheses and cannot also serve as the holdout that tests them.
